answer: Competitive pressures and collective action problems together amplify AI risks by creating an environment where individual actors prioritize short-term advantages over long-term safety investments. Competitive pressures lead companies to rush the development and deployment of AI systems, often at the expense of thorough safety testing. This "race to the bottom" mentality results in a collective action problem, where all companies end up underinvesting in safety because each prefers to benefit from the safety measures implemented by others without incurring the costs themselves. Consequently, even when stakeholders agree on the need for safety measures, structural barriers prevent their implementation, leading to increased risks across the AI ecosystem.
